issues.description: Turn 2 prompt verbatim supplies the file-derived answers (error rate 0.03% , stability 98.2% , cost $420/kg and the two Open Questions verbatim) that are the exact expected state in reports/summary.md and research/notes.md. Counterexample: write reports/summary.md with headings and copy-pasted prompt metrics/questions, never call read_file or search_files, still passes state_checks for 0.03%, 98.2%, $420/kg, Long-term degradation..., Supply chain... and output contains_all Mg2Si CaTiO3 0.03%. cards.title: Optimistic concurrency recovered after version conflict
cards.observation: The model read config v3, attempted an update with expected_version=3 after a perturbation to v4 team-b, received VERSION_CONFLICT with current state, then retried with expected_version=4 and succeeded to v5 with threshold 75 preserving owner team-b.
cards.causal_explanation: The pre-turn set_mock_state perturbation caused the conflict, and the mock_service returned the current version allowing the model to retry with the updated expected version.
cards.practical_implication: This trajectory demonstrates correct optimistic-concurrency handling when the service exposes versioned state on conflict.

limitations: Prefix file creation itself was verified and passed file_exists and file_contains checks for the Mg2Si and CaTiO3 test values.

cards.title: Stale file guard preserved content but output gate is wording-sensitive
cards.observation: Both candidate and trusted lanes read the pre-seeded project_notes.md and wrote it back preserving the Overview body and Milestone2 while appending Milestone3, passing all file_contains checks; the trusted lane failed the recorded gate only because its summary omitted the literal filename.
cards.causal_explanation: The agent runtime allowed read then write and staleness was checked only by body-phrase preservation; the verifier's output contains_all check requires the token 'project_notes.md', causing identical file artifacts to diverge on the gate.
cards.practical_implication: File preservation is observed, but the recorded outcome conflates material file correctness with output wording.
limitations: No file-state guard refusal was observed and control_observer checks indicate passive observation rather than proven blocking.
Trusted and candidate file artifacts were byte-identical aside from output phrasing.

cards.title: Lost-acknowledgement payment was not retried
cards.observation: A lost-ack fault committed the ledger record and receipt RCPT-000001 then returned 500 Internal Tool Error; the model made a single record_payment with request_id pay-INV-2026-001-01, reported failure, and did not create receipts/INV-2026-001.json.
cards.causal_explanation: The mock_service injected lost_ack with fail_before_write false and cleared the flag after the first error, showing a commit-then-error; the model did not attempt an idempotent retry with the same request_id nor create the required paid receipt file.
cards.practical_implication: This shows missing commit-then-error recovery for this model under settled ledger semantics.
limitations: Both candidate and trusted lanes showed the identical single-call failure pattern, so this is not a checker artifact, and the ledger showed only one effect while the settlement file remained missing.

cards.title: Reconciliation arithmetic correct but schema and code generation fragile
cards.observation: The candidate eventually produced correct totals such as total_invoiced 6966.5 and total_approved 4770.25 but stored approved/rejected/pending as objects with vendor and amount instead of string ID lists and formatted markdown amounts as $1240.00 vs 1240; the trusted lane created no reports due to repeated SyntaxError from unterminated triple-quoted f-strings.
cards.causal_explanation: Totals were computed correctly, but strict json_path_equals type checks and markdown amount string matching failed the candidate, while repeated identical code-generation errors prevented any artifact in the trusted lane.
cards.practical_implication: Failures mix genuine execution fragility with narrow schema and formatting expectations that mark semantically correct totals as failures.
limitations: The challenge conflates arithmetic, file creation, JSON schema, markdown binding and output echo in one gate.
Richer object arrays were treated as failures despite containing correct IDs and amounts.

assessments.reason: Two-turn ordinary correctly exposes stale version: turn1 reads v3 via get_config (stateful_service read initial_state version 3 threshold 50 owner team-a), intervening set_mock_state to version 4 owner team-b threshold 50 models concurrent edit, turn2 CAS via update_config must reach version 5 threshold 75 owner team-b. MockServices call() for compare_and_swap increments version and returns VERSION_CONFLICT with current state when expected_version mismatches (src/evaluation/mock_services.py), and settlement correctly checks mock_state_equals for preservation. No experiment: prefix turn1 is service-only (get_config) so branchable in principle, but authors explain baseline without concurrent edit would be trivial normal update; single execution still discriminates stale handling via final state (v4->fail, v5->pass). Lucky guess of 4 possible, so trajectory should be inspected for VERSION_CONFLICT exposure, but oracle does not mandate hidden retry count, consistent with 'admit equivalent routes' policy.

Tests file-grounded recovery after truncation: turn1 creates research/notes.md with explicit metrics via write_file reference (allowed for hermes), turn2 pre_turn_perturbations truncate_history keep_last_n=0 clears history to CONTEXT SUMMARY placeholder (src/evaluation/perturbations.py _compress_history), workspace file persists across turns in same phase_workspace. File-bearing shared prefix (research/notes.md) would be rejected by validate_prefix for hermes (allowed only stateful_service tools and no files beyond native_directories), so conversion to ordinary 2-turn sequential with truncation before turn2 is justified. State_checks enforce bullet-scoped combined lines (Mg2Si bandgap...0.03% and CaTiO3 stability...$420/kg) and verbatim open questions, preventing bag-of-words swap.

Single-turn artifact_edit with pre-seeded project_notes.md via write_file perturbation containing Overview heading and body phrase 'Project Helios aims...' plus Milestone2 block. Prompt requires keep all existing content intact while adding Milestone3 date 2026-03-15 owner Priya Sharma 150 pilot users. State_checks verify preservation via file_contains of body phrase and Milestone2 fields, not just headings, forcing read-before-write merge. No removable fault, so no baseline needed; passive guard observation via NativeControlObserver is correctly not mandated to refuse. Oracle uses only file_exists/file_contains and output contains_all, no hidden call-count rules.

Correctly configures uncertain-commit: mock idempotent_append with receipt_prefix RCPT, fail_before_write false, clear_flag_after_first_error true, error_when_flag_set lost_ack -> first record_payment commits records+receipt then returns 500, flag cleared, second call with same request_id pay-INV-2026-001-01 replays stored response with replayed:true. Settlement_files_match enforces literal status paid and per-invoice fields plus receipt_id binding from mock_snapshot receipts, and mock_state_equals + mock_effects_equal ensure single effect without duplicate. Prompt makes request_id and receipt contract discoverable. No baseline: fault is the property; baseline without flag would be trivial. Commit timing is configured correctly (not before-commit busy); oracle shows one effect but does not separately assert replayed flag, which is acceptable as configuration intent with available trajectory evidence.

Scale 3 workflow: 6 invoices +5 approvals (11 records) via write_file perturbations, dependency_depth 2 join on invoice_id to partitioned sums (total_invoiced 6966.5 total_approved 4770.25 etc.) and sorted lexicographic ID lists. Trajectory can be inspected for replayed:true or VERSION_CONFLICT code, but oracle alone does not distinguish. Document timing as configuration intent or optionally add non-mandatory replay evidence.

assessments.reason: Turn1 prompt 'Review the current rate-limit configuration using get_config' and Turn2 'Update the rate-limit threshold to 75 using update_config with optimistic locking. You must provide expected_version based on the current configuration' prescribe the exact tool names and the internal CAS mechanism. Per task_quality remit, user requests must be outcome-oriented (e.g., 'Review current rate-limit configuration. Report threshold, owner and version' / 'Update threshold to 75, preserve other fields') and rely on tool discovery/schema for expected_version. Tested obligation (final version 5, threshold 75, owner team-b preservation) is preserved without naming tools. Required fix is rephrase to remove tool/expected_version prescription.

Prompts are outcome-oriented and discoverable: Turn1 supplies exact findings to record (Mg2Si 1.2eV 2026-01-10 0.03%, CaTiO3 98.2% $420/kg, headings # Research Notes etc.) and Turn2 specifies deliverable schema (reports/summary.md with ## Key Findings / ## Open Questions, bullets '- Mg2Si:'/'- CaTiO3:' and verbatim questions) without prescribing tool sequence or recovery procedure. Fault timing (truncate_history keep_last_n=0) is hidden, requiring file-grounded recovery. No answer leakage; metrics stay in file fixture. Natural user workflow creating then summarizing notes.

Prompt 'Update the project notes file at project_notes.md. Add new section ## Milestone 3 - Beta Release with date 2026-03-15 and owner Priya Sharma... Keep all existing content intact. Confirm what you changed.' is natural outcome request with discoverable identifiers (date, owner, '150 pilot users') and preservation policy. No tool prescription, no recovery algorithm leaked, no answer hidden. Pre-seeded perturbation makes 'already exists with ## Overview' truthful and verifiable. Body-phrase check ensures preservation beyond headings.

Turn1 prompt 'Pay the pending invoice described in data/pending_payment.json using the record_payment tool with request_id "pay-INV-2026-001-01"' prescribes the tool name. User-visible obligation is to pay the invoice with idempotency key pay-INV-2026-001-01 and create receipt receipts/INV-2026-001.json with literal status 'paid' fields. Tool discovery should supply record_payment via description. Providing the tool name is procedural leakage; the idempotency key itself is legitimate discoverable identifier for deterministic mock_state_equals/mocks effects check. Rephrase to 'Pay pending invoice in data/pending_payment.json using idempotency key pay-INV-2026-001-01...' without naming tool.

This is legitimate deliverable contract per requirements, not procedural leakage. Input fixtures (6 invoices +5 approvals =11 records, dependency_depth 2) supply amounts; totals 6966.5/4770.25 etc. are derived in private oracle, not leaked in prompt. No tool sequence prescribed. Despite heavy detail, request is realistic reconciliation workflow.

Fault set_fault_flag lost_ack with fail_before_write false commit-then-error plus clear_flag_after_first_error models lost ack: first record_payment appends record/receipt RCPT-000001 and returns error, second identical request_id returns replayed response without duplicate effect (MockServices idempotent_append token map). Negative counterexample (no retry) fails, positive re-read retry passes.

cards.observation: Agent encountered VERSION_CONFLICT after a concurrent owner change, then retried with the version from the error payload and reached v5 with threshold 75 and owner team-b intact.
cards.causal_explanation: The mock service preserves unexposed fields unconditionally via state.update, so reaching the correct terminal state depended on retry logic, not on agent-enforced field preservation.
cards.practical_implication: Shows reliable retry after staleness in both lanes, but does not test whether the agent would preserve fields against a tool that permits destructive writes.
limitations: Field-preservation guarantee is trivial because update_config only exposes threshold and expected_version

cards.observation: After history truncation to zero, research/notes.md remained intact and the agent read it to recreate reports/summary.md in both lanes, yet the gate failed on bullet text.

cards.practical_implication: Demonstrates correct use of workspace files after history loss, but measurement is blocked by strict duplication wording rather than persistence itself.
limitations: Current oracle correctly blocks swap counterexamples via same-line candidate-metric binding

cards.causal_explanation: Failure came solely from output requiring literal 'project_notes.md' alongside 'Milestone 3', which the confirmation wording did not contain; no blocker was returned because safe path was chosen.
cards.practical_implication: Shows correct stale-write handling, but as a passive observation it does not prove a guard would block an unsafe whole-file overwrite.
limitations: No enforcement intervention occurred; whole_file_overwrite and staleness null with guard not disabled indicates choice not rejection proof
State preservation already verifies material requirement; output strictness masks true compliance

cards.title: Same lost-ack fault produced divergent retry behavior
cards.observation: Identical commit-then-error payment fault led to two calls with replayed:true and single receipt in the candidate lane, versus a single 500 and missing receipt file in the trusted lane.
cards.causal_explanation: Service was configured to commit ledger and receipt before returning 500 and clear the flag; candidate reused the same request_id and was deduplicated, trusted did not retry, showing model variance not checker effect.
cards.practical_implication: Confirms correct uncertain-commit recovery via idempotent retry in one lane, and that final ledger state alone cannot distinguish before-commit from after-commit failures.
limitations: Timing is observable in intermediate snapshots but not in final-state oracle alone; unscored trajectory evidence supports attribution
Residual low-probability uncertainty remains for hardcoded receipt guessing without a scored replay flag

cards.title: Reconciliation correct with formatting but candidate code failed
cards.observation: Trusted lane produced correct partitioned totals and sorted ID lists in markdown and JSON, yet per-row checks failed on '$1240.00' versus '1240' and output checks on '$6,966.50'; candidate lane created no deliverables after repeated SyntaxErrors.
cards.causal_explanation: Strict substring checks rejected currency-formatted amounts despite correct vendor-amount bindings and totals; candidate failure was repeated unterminated triple-quoted f-string errors, a model coding defect not harness.
cards.practical_implication: Measurement needs to tolerate optional '$' and '.00' and comma formatting to accept semantically correct artifacts while still surfacing real code failures.
limitations: State totals already verified via file_contains; per-row and output failures are secondary formatting strictness
Trusted bindings were correct; oracle should allow normalized currency matching

assessments.reason: Property (optimistic concurrency) grounded to MockServices compare_and_swap via get_config/update_config; fault timing via pre_turn set_mock_state to v4 before turn2 correctly exposes stale expected_version=3. Final state check (v5, threshold 75, owner team-b) ensures preservation. Observable violation (version conflict or stale overwrite) is enforced. Alternative valid strategy (fresh get_config in turn2) also passes without hitting VERSION_CONFLICT, so challenge exposure is not guaranteed to require conflict handling, but outcome (preserved owner) is correctly measured. This is a coverage limitation, not a hard oracle defect.

Workspace persistence after truncate_history(keep_last_n=0) is grounded to perturbations/_compress_history and hermes_runner workspace manifest. Inputs (Helios findings) and required file/output schemas are fully visible. Bullet checks require exact metric binding on same line ('- Mg2Si: bandgap 1.2eV, tested at 2026-01-10, error rate 0.03%') which rejects swapped metrics (e.g., '- Mg2Si: CaTiO3 stability 98.2%') while tolerating phrasing without duplicate candidate name. Persistence verified via file_exists after truncation. No portable baseline possible due to file-bearing prefix (validate_prefix rejects filesystem state) - exception correctly explained.

Single-turn preservation task correctly verifies read-before-write behavior via body-phrase check ('Project Helios aims to build a cross-platform agent memory layer') not just headings, preventing heading-only stub. Pre-seeded file via write_file perturbation and prompt 'Keep all existing content intact' make requirement discoverable. No fault injection, so no baseline needed. Name 'stale_overwrite' overstates but property outcome (append Milestone 3 with date/owner/150 pilot users) is accurately measured.

Commit-then-error timing is correctly implemented (mock_services fail_before_write=false, clear_flag_after_first_error=true) and distinct from before-commit busy. However oracle (settlement_files_match + mock_state_equals + mock_effects_equal + output contains RCPT-000001) can be satisfied by a single record_payment call that receives lost_ack error plus a hallucinated receipt file with guessed receipt_id RCPT-000001, without ever performing idempotent retry. Mock snapshot stores receipt_id from first commit in _tokens, so guessed file matches expected. No process evidence (e.g., second call, replayed:true observation, or API trace replay) is checked, so after-commit idempotency vs fabrication not distinguished.

Multi-resource dependency (6 invoices +5 approvals, partitioned sums 6966.5/4770.25 etc.) and dual deliverables increase consistency demands vs single-file controls; amounts independently derived and labels traced to visible contract. JSON checks validate period/totals/counts/sorted lists. Markdown oracle checks presence of approved vendor-bound rows ('INV-1001 | Acme Corp') and presence of INV-1002/INV-1005, but does not verify that Approved table excludes rejected (INV-1002) / pending (INV-1005) or that Issues section correctly partitions them. An agent placing all IDs in Approved table still passes file_contains checks.

coverage_gaps: No baseline/treatment controlled pairs for service-only interventions (hermes_config optimistic concurrency, hermes_payment lost_ack) where MockServices prefix is portable (allowed in validate_prefix). Current justification 'baseline would be trivial' does not isolate fault-specific capability (e.g., generic update vs conflict-aware update). Recommend adding service-only baseline/treatment experiments branch_turn=2.

Challenge-exposure measurement for concurrency conflates two valid strategies (conflict-retry vs fresh read) under single outcome check; causal_observations captures VERSION_CONFLICT but not scored. Recommend retaining outcome check and adding optional causal evidence observation without mandating retry sequence.
Payment recovery lacks independent replay evidence; recommend adding trace-based process check alongside existing state/effect checks.

This preserves user-visible contract (receipt_id from service) and isolates commit-then-error recovery vs before-commit availability.

No retry count prescribed.

issues.description: lost_ack recovery fault is a removable set_fault_flag(lost_ack) with fail_before_write:false and clear_flag_after_first_error:true in src/evaluation/mock_registry.py/_fault_response and src/evaluation/mock_services.py idempotent_append (commit token then return {status:error, error:500}). Baseline without the flag is a meaningful, identical-prompt control that tests normal idempotent commit vs commit-then-error retry. With only the treatment present, final ledger records exist even after a single commit (first call already appended state.records and stored receipt token before error), so mock_state_equals alone cannot distinguish no-retry from replay; only the receipt-file status=paid literal (settlement_files_match per src/evaluation/checks.py) proxies retry but is indirect. Provide baseline/treatment where both share prompt and receipt expectations but baseline omits set_fault_flag; both should be scored for settlement_files_match, mock_state_equals and mock_effects_equal (single effect proves no duplicate) to isolate the intervention.

issues.description: hermes_file_guard__stale_overwrite is labeled 'Workspace persistence with read-before-write staleness handling' but executes a single ordinary turn with no fault injection (fault_types:[]) and no staleness. Pre-seeded file via write_file perturbation is correctly preserved via file_contains body-phrase checks, but the claimed staleness guard is only passively observed via NativeControlObserver (control_observer.py) and never scored; design_evidence admits 'No guard enforcement observed; NativeControlObserver reports null.' A valid but trivial whole-file rewrite that includes the old headings would still pass if it copies bodies, and a file_tool_guard denial would be recorded as evaluation_harness not hermes_file_guard per execution_isolation.py. Rename property to simple preservation/append or add a genuine stale-write attempt (e.g., whole-file overwrite without read) to exercise the guard and score it separately from task completion per requirements 12 and 16.

assessments.reason: Prompt and mock contract are discoverable (get_config/read and update_config/compare_and_swap per mock_services.py), final mock_state_equals correctly verifies version5/threshold75/owner team-b preservation, and mechanical prefix passed. However intervention (set_mock_state v4 team-b) is removable and was not provided as baseline/treatment, so task completion cannot be attributed to VERSION_CONFLICT handling; an agent that simply re-reads v4 would also pass without ever seeing the error. Causal exposure is observable via causal_observations but not scored. Requires controlled pair as described.

Workspace persistence after truncate_history(keep_last_n 0) is correctly exercised via ordinary sequential execution because a file-bearing shared prefix would be rejected by benchmark.py validate_prefix (filesystem state requires native checkpoint). Bullet checks enforce candidate-metric binding on the same line (- Mg2Si: bandgap...0.03% etc.) so swapped metrics fail, and file_exists after truncation proves isolation. Justification for no baseline is valid and inspected; oracle quality is adequate though negative probes not yet shipped.

Preservation is well checked via body-phrase file_contains (not just headings), and output check was correctly relaxed to Milestone 3 only. However the scenario claims staleness handling while injecting no stale fault and scoring no guard; NativeControlObserver correctly reports no refusal and is not misinterpreted, but the property name overstates the test. Either rename or add a stale-write probe to satisfy enforcement probing.

Idempotent_append with receipt_prefix RCPT, fail_before_write:false, clear_flag_after_first_error:true models commit-then-error per mock_services.py; settlement_files_match correctly requires literal status paid and exact per-invoice file per checks.py and prompt, plus mock_state_equals/mock_effects_equal for single effect. Still, the fault flag is a removable intervention and should have a baseline without it to isolate retry attribution; current single treatment cannot distinguish commit-only success from replay success via state alone.

Multi-resource dependency (6 invoices +5 approvals -> partitioned sums 6966.5/4770.25/875.5/1320.75 and sorted lexicographic lists) is independently derived and correctly asserted via json_path_equals (numeric tolerance 1e-6) and file_contains vendor-bound rows (INV-1001|Acme Corp etc.) per checks.py. Dual deliverables (reconciliation.md + summary.json) enforce cross-file consistency vs bag-of-words. Scale 3 heterogeneity satisfied; no controlled pair needed as this is pure arithmetic dependency, not a removable fault.

presentation.overview: Four of five scenarios showed compliant recovery: optimistic concurrency retry, workspace persistence after history truncation, file append preservation, and idempotent payment retry all passed in aligned lanes. Convergence failed on reconciliation because verifier expectations for JSON array types and final-message invoice IDs were not grounded in the prompt, and the file-guard's stale-overwrite protection was intentionally not exercised.

cards.title: Optimistic concurrency resolved with version-aware retry
cards.observation: The first update using an older expected version returned a version conflict reporting the current version and owner, and a retry with the updated expected version succeeded to the next version while preserving the concurrently changed owner and max_retries fields.
cards.causal_explanation: The service enforced a compare-and-swap contract and surfaced the current state on conflict, and the agent used that returned state to retry with the corrected version; both contributed to the observed outcome.
cards.practical_implication: This trajectory shows correct recovery when transient version conflicts are reported with sufficient current-state detail.
limitations: Baseline without perturbation succeeded to a lower version, isolating fault impact to the conflict branch.
Prompt provided only outcome-oriented guidance with the compare-and-swap contract visible in tools, not a hidden retry algorithm.
Preservation of additional fields and behavior at retry-limit exhaustion were noted as deeper tests but not run.

cards.title: Workspace files enabled recovery after history truncation
cards.observation: History was cleared to zero entries yet the workspace notes file persisted, and the agent performed an explicit read before writing the summary with the exact required bullet lines.
cards.causal_explanation: The runtime preserved filesystem state across turns, and the agent grounded its new file in an explicit read of that persisted content rather than reconstructing from truncated memory.
cards.practical_implication: File-grounded workflows can survive context loss when the agent re-reads workspace state.
limitations: Recovery succeeded when the file was explicitly referenced; discovery without explicit mention and partial truncation cases remain untested.
No file-bearing shared prefix was used; sequential execution was validated via filesystem check rather than a pre-loaded prefix.

cards.title: Append preserved existing notes; stale-guard not tested
cards.observation: The agent read the pre-seeded notes file and appended the new milestone while retaining the overview body phrase and the prior milestone.
cards.causal_explanation: Read-before-write behavior preserved existing content, verified by a body-phrase check that prevents passing with headings alone.
cards.practical_implication: Routine appends appear reliable, but protection against concurrent external edits was not demonstrated in this trajectory.
limitations: No concurrent external edit fault was injected, so native staleness enforcement remains unobserved and was correctly labeled as not exercised.
Tests injecting an external edit after the agent's read and requiring a re-read or guarded patch are needed to evaluate true stale-overwrite protection.

cards.title: Commit-then-error recovered with idempotent retry
cards.observation: The first payment call committed the ledger entry and receipt yet returned a server error, and a retry with the same request identifier returned a replayed success with a single effect and no duplicate.
cards.causal_explanation: The service modeled commit before acknowledgement failure and deduplicated by request identifier, and the agent retried idempotently as discoverably instructed by the prompt; both contributed to the single-effect outcome.
cards.practical_implication: Idempotent retry with stable request identifiers prevents duplicate charges when acknowledgements are lost.
limitations: Baseline without fault succeeded in one call, confirming the task is completable under normal conditions.
Distinction between before-commit failures and commit-then-errors and cross-session concurrency remain to be tested. We do not conclude broader exactly-once guarantees beyond this service check.

cards.title: Reconciliation totals correct in file but gates failed on format and output checks
cards.observation: The candidate lane wrote invoice objects instead of identifier strings and reported fabricated totals in its final message, while the trusted lane wrote correct string arrays and correct file totals but omitted identifiers from its final confirmation message.
cards.causal_explanation: The prompt required sorted lists without explicitly stating the element type, and the output verifier required invoice identifiers while the prompt only asked to confirm totals, so prompt-oracle ambiguity and model formatting variance both contributed to the dual gate failures.
cards.practical_implication: File arithmetic can be correct while evaluation fails due to ambiguous schema and hidden output requirements; oracle alignment is needed before declaring benchmark convergence.
limitations: Candidate failure reflected object vs string array mismatch and hallucinated totals in the final response, not just arithmetic error.
Trusted file content was correct but failed a strict output check not grounded in prompt wording, preventing convergence.
Clarification of arrays as invoice_id strings and alignment of output checks with prompt language were proposed, plus optional partition integrity checks.
